---
title: "Annotation concordance"
subtitle: "Do the automated annotators agree with each other?"
format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 3
    # MUST be true. With embed-resources:false quarto writes widget JS to a
    # sibling `site_libs/` directory, and NO module publishes that directory --
    # so every plotly widget rendered BLANK in the published report while the
    # HTML itself looked fine. Self-contained is the only form that survives
    # publishDir copying the .html on its own.
    embed-resources: true
    code-fold: true
    code-tools: true
params:
  celltypist_obs: "NO_FILE"
  sctype_object: "NO_FILE"
  azimuth_object: "NO_FILE"
  project_name: "project"
  work_directory: "."
  min_pair_cells: 20
---

<!--
This notebook exists because the pipeline runs up to three independent cell-type
annotators on the SAME input object, in parallel, and then never compares them.
Each writes its own report claiming its own labels. Nothing in the pipeline ever
asked whether they agree, so a disagreement on a third of the cells would have
been completely invisible.

That is the same failure mode as the CNV callers (inferCNV vs SCEVAN disagreeing
on 649 of 1,683 cells with no report saying so).

sc-best-practices' annotation chapter asks for exactly these diagnostics:
crosstab of manual vs automated labels, uncertainty/confidence scores per cell
type, and flagging low-confidence cells as Unknown.
-->


```{r load, include = FALSE}
is_real <- function(p) {
  !is.null(p) && !is.na(p) && nzchar(p) && !grepl("NO_FILE", p) && file.exists(p)
}

# Each annotator writes a different column name. Order matters: the first match
# wins. The column this pipeline actually writes is listed FIRST in each vector;
# the rest are fallbacks for objects produced by a stock Seurat/Azimuth workflow.
#
# `sctype` is the major-class call and is deliberately preferred over the
# aggregated `scytpe_subset`: `sctype` is what the rest of the pipeline consumes
# (--celltype_col sctype), so it is the label whose disagreement actually
# propagates downstream.
#
# Azimuth's column is `azimuth_labels` (plural) -- notebook_azimuth.qmd renames
# TransferData's `predicted.id` to it. Getting this name wrong does not fail; it
# silently drops the annotator, which is the exact class of bug this module was
# written to catch.
LABEL_CANDIDATES <- list(
  celltypist = c("majority_voting", "predicted_labels", "celltypist_cell_label_coarse"),
  sctype     = c("sctype", "scytpe_subset", "sctype_aggregate", "cell_type",
                 "sctype_classification", "customclassif", "sctype_major"),
  azimuth    = c("azimuth_labels", "predicted.celltype.l2", "predicted.celltype.l1",
                 "predicted.id", "predicted_celltype", "azimuth_label")
)

# Per-cell confidence, where the annotator emits one. These are NOT on a common
# scale -- CellTypist's `conf_score` is a classifier probability, Azimuth's
# `prediction.score.max` is the best label-transfer score -- so they are reported
# side by side and never pooled or subtracted. scType emits no per-cell score.
CONF_CANDIDATES <- list(
  celltypist = c("conf_score", "celltypist_conf_score_coarse"),
  sctype     = character(0),
  azimuth    = c("prediction.score.max", "predicted.celltype.l2.score", "predicted.id.score")
)

# What each score MEANS, so the report can say it rather than assume the reader knows.
CONF_MEANING <- c(
  CellTypist = "logistic-regression probability for the winning class",
  Azimuth    = "highest per-label reference-mapping transfer score"
)

pick_from <- function(nms, cands) {
  hit <- intersect(cands, nms)
  if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_character_
}
pick_label <- function(nms, which) pick_from(nms, LABEL_CANDIDATES[[which]])
pick_conf  <- function(nms, which) pick_from(nms, CONF_CANDIDATES[[which]])

labels  <- list()     # name -> data.table(cell_id, label)
conf    <- list()     # name -> data.table(cell_id, conf_score)  (annotators that emit one)
conf_col <- list()    # name -> the column the score came from, for the methods note
extra   <- list()     # side-channel info (clusters)
dropped <- list()     # annotator -> why it contributed nothing, for reporting

# --- CellTypist: obs.csv exported by sceasy -------------------------------
ct_path <- params$celltypist_obs
if (is_real(ct_path) && dir.exists(ct_path)) ct_path <- file.path(ct_path, "obs.csv")
if (is_real(ct_path)) {
  obs <- fread(ct_path)
  # The index column is written unnamed; fread calls it V1.
  idcol <- names(obs)[1]
  setnames(obs, idcol, "cell_id")
  lc <- pick_label(names(obs), "celltypist")
  if (is.na(lc)) {
    dropped$CellTypist <- sprintf(
      "its obs.csv has none of the expected label columns (%s); it has: %s",
      paste(LABEL_CANDIDATES$celltypist, collapse = ", "),
      paste(head(names(obs), 25), collapse = ", "))
  }
  if (!is.na(lc)) {
    labels$CellTypist <- obs[, .(cell_id = as.character(cell_id), label = as.character(get(lc)))]
    cc <- pick_conf(names(obs), "celltypist")
    if (!is.na(cc)) {
      conf$CellTypist <- obs[, .(cell_id = as.character(cell_id),
                                 conf_score = as.numeric(get(cc)))]
      conf_col$CellTypist <- cc
    }
    ccl <- intersect(c("seurat_clusters", "cluster"), names(obs))
    if (length(ccl))
      extra$cluster <- obs[, .(cell_id = as.character(cell_id), cluster = as.character(get(ccl[1])))]
  }
}

# --- Seurat-based annotators ---------------------------------------------
# Returns the labels, or a `why` attribute explaining why there are none. An
# object that was supplied but yielded nothing must be REPORTED, never dropped
# in silence -- a silently missing annotator turns a three-way cross-check into
# a two-way one with no trace in the report.
read_seurat_labels <- function(path, which) {
  fail <- function(why) structure(list(), class = "conc_fail", why = why)
  if (!is_real(path)) return(NULL)                       # genuinely not supplied
  if (!requireNamespace("Seurat", quietly = TRUE))
    return(fail("the Seurat package is not available in this container"))
  obj <- tryCatch(readRDS(path), error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
  if (is.character(obj)) return(fail(sprintf("the object could not be read (%s)", obj)))
  md <- tryCatch(obj@meta.data, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(md)) return(fail("the object has no @meta.data slot"))
  lc <- pick_label(names(md), which)
  if (is.na(lc)) return(fail(sprintf(
    "its metadata has none of the expected label columns (%s); it has: %s",
    paste(LABEL_CANDIDATES[[which]], collapse = ", "),
    paste(head(names(md), 30), collapse = ", "))))
  out <- data.table(cell_id = rownames(md), label = as.character(md[[lc]]))
  # Carry the per-cell score along when the object has one; `take()` splits it off.
  cc <- pick_conf(names(md), which)
  if (!is.na(cc)) {
    out[, conf_score := as.numeric(md[[cc]])]
    setattr(out, "conf_col", cc)
  }
  out
}

take <- function(res, name) {
  if (is.null(res)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (inherits(res, "conc_fail")) {
    dropped[[name]] <<- attr(res, "why")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  if ("conf_score" %in% names(res)) {
    conf[[name]]     <<- res[, .(cell_id, conf_score)]
    conf_col[[name]] <<- attr(res, "conf_col")
    res <- res[, .(cell_id, label)]
  }
  labels[[name]] <<- res
  invisible(NULL)
}

take(read_seurat_labels(params$sctype_object, "sctype"),   "scType")
take(read_seurat_labels(params$azimuth_object, "azimuth"), "Azimuth")

n_ann <- length(labels)
```

```{r dropped-annotators, results = 'asis'}
if (length(dropped)) {
  scratch_finding(
    paste0(
      "**", length(dropped), " annotator output(s) were supplied to this report but ",
      "contributed no labels**, so the comparison below is narrower than the run ",
      "actually was:\n\n",
      paste(sprintf("- **%s** -- %s", names(dropped), unlist(dropped)), collapse = "\n"),
      "\n\nThis is a wiring problem, not a biological result. Fix the label-column ",
      "name in `LABEL_CANDIDATES` and re-run: a cross-check that quietly drops one ",
      "of the methods being cross-checked is worse than no cross-check at all."),
    type = "important", title = "Annotator supplied but not readable")
}
```

```{r no-data, results = 'asis'}
  scratch_finding(
    sprintf(paste("Only **%d** annotator produced labels, so there is nothing to compare.",
                  "Concordance needs at least two of CellTypist, scType and Azimuth.",
                  "Enable a second annotator to get a cross-check on the cell-type calls."),
            n_ann),
    type = "caution", title = "Not enough annotators")
}
```

```{r build-joint, include = FALSE}
if (n_ann >= 2) {
  # Cell IDs can carry an annotator-specific prefix. Harmonise by stripping a
  # leading "<sample>." or "<sample>_" ONLY when that makes the sets overlap --
  # a silent zero-overlap join is the exact bug that made the CNV consensus run
  # on one caller for weeks.
  norm_id <- function(x) sub("^[^._]+[._]", "", x)

  ids <- lapply(labels, function(d) d$cell_id)
  raw_ov <- length(Reduce(intersect, ids))
  nrm_ov <- length(Reduce(intersect, lapply(ids, norm_id)))
  used_norm <- nrm_ov > raw_ov
  # The confidence tables are keyed on the SAME ids and must be rewritten too,
  # or every later merge against them silently returns zero rows.
  if (used_norm) {
    labels <- lapply(labels, function(d) { d[, cell_id := norm_id(cell_id)]; d })
    conf   <- lapply(conf,   function(d) { d[, cell_id := norm_id(cell_id)]; d })
  }

  joint <- Reduce(function(a, b) merge(a, b, by = "cell_id"),
                  Map(function(d, n) { x <- copy(d); setnames(x, "label", n); x },
                      labels, names(labels)))
  overlap <- nrow(joint)
}
```

```{r overlap-check, results = 'asis'}
if (n_ann >= 2 && overlap == 0) {
  scratch_finding(
    paste("The annotators share **no cell IDs**, so no comparison is possible.",
          "This is almost always a naming mismatch (a sample prefix applied by one",
          "annotator and not another), not a genuine absence of shared cells."),
    type = "important", title = "Zero cell overlap")
}
```

## Pairwise agreement

```{r pairwise, results = 'asis'}
if (n_ann >= 2 && overlap > 0) {
  anns  <- names(labels)
  pairs <- combn(anns, 2, simplify = FALSE)

  # Two annotators can be right and still disagree textually, so normalise
  # before calling anything a conflict.
  #
  # Dropping a trailing "cell"/"cells" token is NOT cosmetic. Without it,
  # CellTypist's "Epithelial cells" and Azimuth's "Epithelial" scored as a
  # disagreement on 4,699 cells -- the single largest block in this report --
  # and the pair's agreement read 7.9% when it is really 28.1%. The optional
  # space also catches the unspaced "Tcells" form.
  #
  # It stops at ONE trailing token on purpose: "B_Plasma_Cells" -> "b plasma"
  # must NOT collapse onto "B cell" -> "b", because merging B and plasma cells
  # into one class is a real difference of resolution, not a spelling.
  canon <- function(x) {
    x <- tolower(trimws(as.character(x)))
    x <- gsub("[_/.-]+", " ", x)
    x <- gsub("\\s+", " ", trimws(x))
    stripped <- sub("\\s*cells?$", "", x)
    x <- ifelse(nzchar(stripped), stripped, x)   # a bare "cell" stays "cell"
    sub("s$", "", x)
  }

  # How much of the raw disagreement was only ever spelling. Reported, not hidden:
  # a reader who sees "28.1% agree" deserves to know it was 7.9% before names
  # were harmonised, and on which labels.
  canon_raw <- function(x) {
    x <- tolower(trimws(as.character(x)))
    sub("s$", "", gsub("\\s+", " ", gsub("[_/.-]+", " ", x)))
  }

  UNCALLED <- c("unknown", "unassigned", "na", "")

  # Raw label-identity agreement is only meaningful between annotators working
  # at the SAME resolution. One method calling "B_Plasma_Cells" where another
  # says "B cell" / "Plasma cell" is a difference of resolution, not of opinion,
  # and scoring it as a disagreement would report a real biological consensus as
  # a conflict. `nesting` measures the alternative question -- does the finer
  # partition sit INSIDE the coarser one? -- by taking, for each fine label, the
  # share of its cells that land in that label's single most common coarse
  # class. High nesting with low agreement means the two methods concur and
  # simply disagree about how many names to use.
  nesting_purity <- function(fine, coarse) {
    d <- data.table(f = fine, c = coarse)[, .N, by = .(f, c)]
    sum(d[, max(N), by = f]$V1) / max(1, length(fine))
  }

  res <- rbindlist(lapply(pairs, function(p) {
    a <- canon(joint[[p[1]]]); b <- canon(joint[[p[2]]])
    a_out <- is.na(a) | a %in% UNCALLED
    b_out <- is.na(b) | b %in% UNCALLED
    known <- !a_out & !b_out
    na <- uniqueN(a[known]); nb <- uniqueN(b[known])
    # Whichever side resolves more types is the "fine" one for the nesting test.
    nest <- if (sum(known) == 0) NA_real_
            else if (na >= nb) nesting_purity(a[known], b[known])
            else nesting_purity(b[known], a[known])
    # Same comparison without the name harmonisation, to size its effect.
    ar <- canon_raw(joint[[p[1]]]); br <- canon_raw(joint[[p[2]]])
    agree_raw <- sum(ar[known] == br[known])
    data.table(pair = paste(p[1], "vs", p[2]),
               compared = sum(known),
               agree    = sum(a[known] == b[known]),
               pct      = round(100 * sum(a[known] == b[known]) / max(1, sum(known)), 1),
               naming   = sum(a[known] == b[known]) - agree_raw,
               labels_a = na, labels_b = nb,
               nesting  = round(100 * nest, 1),
               uncalled = sum(a_out | b_out))
  }))
  res[, disagree := compared - agree]
  res[, gran := pmax(labels_a, labels_b) / pmax(1, pmin(labels_a, labels_b))]

  worst <- res[which.min(pct)]
  msg <- sprintf(paste("Across **%s cells** annotated by more than one method,",
                       "%s agree on **%.1f%%** of calls -- they disagree on **%s of %s cells**."),
                 format(overlap, big.mark = ","), worst$pair, worst$pct,
                 format(worst$disagree, big.mark = ","), format(worst$compared, big.mark = ","))

  # A resolution mismatch must not be reported as a contradiction: the remedy is
  # completely different (map the labels, vs. distrust the calls).
  resolution_gap <- !is.na(worst$nesting) && worst$gran >= 1.5 && worst$nesting >= 80
  if (resolution_gap) {
    msg <- paste(msg, sprintf(paste(
      "**Read that number with care -- it is mostly a difference of resolution, not of",
      "opinion.** These two methods resolve **%d** and **%d** distinct types, and **%.1f%%**",
      "of the finer labels nest inside a single coarser class. They largely agree about",
      "what the cells are and disagree about how finely to name them, so the fix is a",
      "label mapping between the two vocabularies, not distrust of the calls."),
      worst$labels_a, worst$labels_b, worst$nesting))
  } else if (worst$pct < 70) {
    msg <- paste(msg,
      "The labels sit at comparable resolution, so this is a genuine conflict rather than",
      "a naming difference. **Below 70% agreement the choice of annotator is itself a",
      "result.** Any downstream analysis keyed on cell type (composition, differential",
      "abundance, cell-cell communication) inherits that choice, so state which annotator",
      "was used and check whether the conclusion survives switching to the other.")
  } else if (worst$pct < 90) {
    msg <- paste(msg,
      "Agreement in the 70-90% band is typical for annotators trained on different",
      "references; the disagreements are usually concentrated in a few related",
      "populations rather than spread evenly -- see the confusion matrix below.")
  }
  if (used_norm) {
    msg <- paste(msg,
      "_Cell IDs were harmonised by stripping a sample prefix to make the label sets joinable._")
  }

  # Naming variation is the first thing a reader suspects, so answer it up front
  # with a number instead of leaving them to wonder.
  if (sum(res$naming) > 0) {
    nw <- res[which.max(naming)]
    msg <- paste(msg, sprintf(paste(
      "_Label names were harmonised before comparing (case, `_`/`-`/`.` separators,",
      "plurals, and a trailing \"cell(s)\" token). That accounts for **%s** of the",
      "matches in %s alone -- e.g. one method writes `Epithelial cells` where the",
      "other writes `Epithelial`. Everything still counted as a disagreement below",
      "is a genuine difference of label, not of spelling._"),
      format(nw$naming, big.mark = ","), nw$pair))
  }

  scratch_finding(msg,
                  type = if (worst$pct < 70 && !resolution_gap) "caution" else "note",
                  title = "Annotator agreement")
  scratch_table(res[, .(pair, compared, agree, disagree, `agreement %` = pct,
                        `same cell type, different name` = naming,
                        `types A` = labels_a, `types B` = labels_b,
                        `nesting %` = nesting, `not compared` = uncalled)],
                caption = paste("Pairwise agreement between annotators.",
                                "`same cell type, different name` = matches that exist only because",
                                "names were harmonised; `nesting %` = share of the finer labels",
                                "contained in a single coarser class; `not compared` = cells at",
                                "least one method left Unknown/unassigned."))
}
```

```{r agreement-figure}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 3.2
if (n_ann >= 2 && overlap > 0) {
  d <- copy(res)
  d[, tip := sprintf("%s\n%.1f%% agreement\n%s of %s cells match",
                     pair, pct, format(agree, big.mark = ","), format(compared, big.mark = ","))]
  ggplot(d, aes(reorder(pair, pct), pct, fill = pct, text = tip)) +
    geom_col(width = .6) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 70, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#8a5a00") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct)), hjust = -.15, size = 3.4) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0b7b3", high = "#0d366b", limits = c(0, 100), guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 105), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .05))) +
    coord_flip() +
    labs(title = "Agreement between annotation methods",
         subtitle = "dashed line = 70%, below which the annotator choice drives downstream results",
         x = NULL, y = "cells with identical label (%)") +
    theme_scratch()
}
```

## Cells one method refused to call

```{r uncalled, results = 'asis'}
# Agreement statistics necessarily exclude cells that a method left Unknown --
# but that exclusion hides the most actionable failure of all. An annotator that
# declines to call 18% of cells which another annotator confidently assigns to a
# single population has a reference gap, and the agreement % it earns on the
# remainder flatters it. This section reports exactly what the denominator drops.
if (n_ann >= 2 && overlap > 0) {
  anns <- names(labels)
  gaps <- rbindlist(lapply(anns, function(a) {
    av <- canon(joint[[a]])
    out <- is.na(av) | av %in% UNCALLED
    if (!sum(out)) return(NULL)
    others <- setdiff(anns, a)
    rbindlist(lapply(others, function(o) {
      ov <- canon(joint[[o]])
      keep <- out & !is.na(ov) & !ov %in% UNCALLED
      if (!sum(keep)) return(NULL)
      tab <- sort(table(joint[[o]][keep]), decreasing = TRUE)
      data.table(annotator = a, uncalled = sum(out), rescued_by = o,
                 rescued = sum(keep), top_label = names(tab)[1],
                 top_n = as.integer(tab[1]))
    }))
  }))

  if (!is.null(gaps) && nrow(gaps)) {
    w <- gaps[which.max(top_n)]
    pct_unc <- 100 * w$uncalled / overlap
    msg <- sprintf(paste(
      "**%s leaves %s of %s shared cells (%.1f%%) Unknown or unassigned.** Those cells are",
      "excluded from every agreement figure above, so they never count against it.",
      "%s does assign **%s** of them, and the single largest block -- **%s cells** -- it calls",
      "**%s**."),
      w$annotator, format(w$uncalled, big.mark = ","), format(overlap, big.mark = ","),
      pct_unc, w$rescued_by, format(w$rescued, big.mark = ","),
      format(w$top_n, big.mark = ","), w$top_label)
    if (pct_unc >= 10) {
      msg <- paste(msg, sprintf(paste(
        "A block this size concentrated on one population is a **reference gap, not",
        "ambiguity**: if %s carried no marker set for %s it cannot call it, and those",
        "cells will be silently missing from any composition or abundance analysis keyed",
        "on %s. Check that population is present in its marker database before using",
        "these labels downstream."), w$annotator, w$top_label, w$annotator))
    }
    scratch_finding(msg, type = if (pct_unc >= 10) "caution" else "note",
                    title = "Uncalled cells")
    scratch_table(gaps[order(-top_n),
                       .(annotator, `cells uncalled` = uncalled, `named by` = rescued_by,
                         `of those, named` = rescued, `largest block` = top_label,
                         cells = top_n)],
                  caption = "What each annotator left uncalled, and what the others made of it")
  }
}
```

## Where they disagree

```{r confusion-figure}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7
if (n_ann >= 2 && overlap > 0) {
  p <- pairs[[which.min(res$pct)]]
  cm <- joint[, .N, by = c(p[1], p[2])]
  setnames(cm, c("A", "B", "n"))
  # Rare label pairs make the heatmap unreadable and are not actionable.
  cm <- cm[n >= params$min_pair_cells]
  if (nrow(cm)) {
    cm[, pct_of_A := 100 * n / sum(n), by = A]
    cm[, tip := sprintf("%s (%s)  ->  %s (%s)\n%s cells, %.1f%% of %s",
                        p[1], A, p[2], B, format(n, big.mark = ","), pct_of_A, A)]
    ggplot(cm, aes(B, A, fill = pct_of_A, text = tip)) +
      geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = .4) +
      scale_fill_gradient(low = "#eef4fd", high = "#0d366b", name = "% of row") +
      labs(title = sprintf("Label correspondence: %s vs %s", p[1], p[2]),
           subtitle = sprintf("row-normalised; pairs with <%d cells omitted", params$min_pair_cells),
           x = p[2], y = p[1]) +
      theme_scratch() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  }
}
```

```{r confusion-table, results = 'asis'}
if (n_ann >= 2 && overlap > 0) {
  p <- pairs[[which.min(res$pct)]]
  # `canon()` is defined once in the pairwise chunk. It used to be redefined
  # here with a slightly different body, which meant the conflict table could
  # disagree with the agreement percentage it was supposed to explain.
  cf <- joint[canon(get(p[1])) != canon(get(p[2])), .N, by = c(p[1], p[2])][order(-N)]
  setnames(cf, c(p[1], p[2], "cells"))
  if (nrow(cf)) {
    top <- head(cf, 3)
    scratch_finding(
      paste0("The largest single disagreement is **",
             format(top$cells[1], big.mark = ","), " cells** that ", p[1], " calls **",
             top[[1]][1], "** and ", p[2], " calls **", top[[2]][1], "**. ",
             "Disagreements concentrated in one pair of related populations are a ",
             "boundary problem (where does one state end and the next begin) rather ",
             "than a failure of either method -- but the boundary is yours to choose."),
      type = "note", title = "Largest disagreement")
    scratch_table(head(cf, 25), caption = "Most frequent label conflicts, largest first")
  }
}
```

## Annotation confidence

```{r conf-prep, include = FALSE}
# Every annotator that emits a per-cell score, not just CellTypist. The scores are
# kept SEPARATE throughout: pooling a logistic-regression probability with a
# reference-mapping transfer score would produce a number that means nothing.
conf_anns <- intersect(names(labels), names(conf))
has_conf  <- length(conf_anns) > 0

if (has_conf) {
  cd <- rbindlist(lapply(conf_anns, function(a) {
    m <- merge(labels[[a]], conf[[a]], by = "cell_id")
    m[, annotator := a][]
  }))
  by_type <- cd[, .(cells = .N,
                    median_conf = as.numeric(round(median(conf_score, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
                    pct_below_half = round(100 * mean(conf_score < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
                by = .(annotator, label)][order(annotator, median_conf)]
  by_ann <- cd[, .(cells = .N,
                   median_conf = as.numeric(round(median(conf_score, na.rm = TRUE), 3)),
                   pct_below_half = round(100 * mean(conf_score < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE), 1)),
               by = annotator]

  # Prepared HERE, not in the figure chunk, because the figure's `fig-height` is
  # computed from `cs_rows` and chunk options are evaluated before the body runs.
  # A fixed height cannot work: this axis is one row per cell type, and the count
  # depends entirely on which annotators and references the run used.
  keep    <- by_type[cells >= params$min_pair_cells]
  cs      <- merge(cd, keep[, .(annotator, label)], by = c("annotator", "label"))
  cs_rows <- nrow(keep)
}
```

```{r conf-finding, results = 'asis'}
if (has_conf) {
  low <- by_type[median_conf < 0.5 & cells >= params$min_pair_cells]

  parts <- vapply(conf_anns, function(a) {
    s <- by_ann[annotator == a]
    meaning <- if (a %in% names(CONF_MEANING)) CONF_MEANING[[a]] else "per-cell score"
    lo <- low[annotator == a]
    txt <- sprintf(paste("- **%s** (`%s`, %s): median **%.3f**, with **%.1f%%** of cells",
                         "below 0.5."),
                   a, conf_col[[a]], meaning, s$median_conf, s$pct_below_half)
    if (nrow(lo)) txt <- paste(txt, sprintf(
      "Weakest population(s): **%s**.", paste(head(lo$label, 4), collapse = ", ")))
    txt
  }, character(1))

  msg <- paste0(
    "Each annotator that reports a per-cell score, scored on its own scale:\n\n",
    paste(parts, collapse = "\n"), "\n\n")

  if (length(conf_anns) > 1) {
    msg <- paste0(msg,
      "**These numbers are not comparable to each other.** A CellTypist probability and ",
      "an Azimuth transfer score answer different questions, so the annotator with the ",
      "higher median is not the better one -- read each against its own 0.5 line, and ",
      "use the comparison below, which asks the one question they can both answer.")
  }
  if (nrow(low)) {
    msg <- paste0(msg,
      "\n\nPopulations whose median score sits below 0.5 should be treated as provisional; ",
      "best practice is to relabel low-confidence cells as `Unknown` rather than carry a ",
      "weak call into downstream analysis.")
  }
  scratch_finding(msg, type = if (nrow(low)) "caution" else "note",
                  title = "Classifier confidence")
  scratch_table(by_type[, .(annotator, label, cells, median_conf,
                            `% below 0.5` = pct_below_half)],
                caption = "Per-cell confidence by predicted cell type, lowest first within each annotator")
}
```

```{r conf-figure}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: !expr if (exists("cs_rows")) max(6, 0.30 * cs_rows + 2.2) else 8
if (has_conf && exists("cs") && nrow(cs)) {
  # Mapped straight to y instead of x + coord_flip(). With coord_flip(),
  # facet_wrap(scales = "free_x") did NOT drop the other annotator's levels, so
  # both panels rendered all 36 cell-type names stacked on top of each other and
  # the axis was unreadable. Faceting the aesthetic the labels actually sit on
  # frees them correctly.
  SEP <- "\u001f"
  ord <- keep[order(annotator, -median_conf)]
  ord[, key := paste(annotator, label, sep = SEP)]
  cs[, key := factor(paste(annotator, label, sep = SEP), levels = ord$key)]
  ggplot(cs, aes(conf_score, key, fill = annotator)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#8a5a00") +
    # 24k outlier dots per panel buried the boxes and forced the figure static.
    # The box, whiskers and the 0.5 line carry the message; the dots did not.
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = .3, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) sub(paste0("^.*", SEP), "", x)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(.02, .02))) +
    facet_wrap(~ annotator, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
    labs(title = "Per-cell confidence by predicted cell type",
         subtitle = sprintf(paste("dashed line = 0.5; types with <%d cells omitted;",
                                  "outliers hidden.\nScales are per-annotator and",
                                  "not comparable across facets"),
                            params$min_pair_cells),
         x = "confidence score (annotator's own scale)", y = NULL) +
    theme_scratch() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
```


```{r conf-vs-uncalled, results = 'asis'}
# The one question the two scores CAN both answer, on a common footing: are the
# cells a third annotator refused to call also the cells the scoring annotators
# found hard? If yes, the Unknowns are genuinely ambiguous cells and every method
# is struggling on them. If no -- confident calls where another method saw
# nothing -- the gap is that method's reference, not the biology, and treating
# its Unknowns as "low quality cells" would be wrong.
if (has_conf && n_ann >= 2 && overlap > 0) {
  jkeys <- intersect(names(joint), names(labels))
  rows <- rbindlist(lapply(conf_anns, function(a) {
    cj <- merge(joint, conf[[a]], by = "cell_id")
    rbindlist(lapply(setdiff(jkeys, a), function(o) {
      ov <- canon(cj[[o]])
      out <- is.na(ov) | ov %in% UNCALLED
      if (sum(out) < params$min_pair_cells || sum(!out) < params$min_pair_cells) return(NULL)
      m_out <- median(cj$conf_score[out],  na.rm = TRUE)
      m_in  <- median(cj$conf_score[!out], na.rm = TRUE)
      pw <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(
              wilcox.test(cj$conf_score[out], cj$conf_score[!out])$p.value),
            error = function(e) NA_real_)
      data.table(scorer = a, uncalled_by = o,
                 n_uncalled = sum(out), n_called = sum(!out),
                 median_on_uncalled = round(m_out, 3), median_on_called = round(m_in, 3),
                 ratio = round(m_out / max(m_in, 1e-9), 2), p_value = pw)
    }))
  }))

  if (!is.null(rows) && nrow(rows)) {
    fmt_p <- function(p) {
      if (is.na(p)) return("")
      if (p < 2.2e-16) return(", Wilcoxon p < 2.2e-16")
      sprintf(", Wilcoxon p = %.3g", p)
    }
    # Report the target ONE annotator's Unknowns at a time: "which cells did X
    # refuse to call" is the question, and every scorer answers it separately.
    tgt   <- rows[, .(n = sum(n_uncalled)), by = uncalled_by][which.max(n)]$uncalled_by
    sub   <- rows[uncalled_by == tgt][order(-ratio)]
    sure  <- sub[ratio >= 0.9]
    unsure <- sub[ratio <  0.9]

    lines <- sprintf(
      "- **%s**: median **%.3f** on those cells vs **%.3f** elsewhere (ratio **%.2f**%s)",
      sub$scorer, sub$median_on_uncalled, sub$median_on_called, sub$ratio,
      vapply(sub$p_value, fmt_p, character(1)))

    msg <- sprintf(paste0(
      "**%s leaves %s cells uncalled.** Every other annotator that reports a per-cell ",
      "score was asked how certain it is about exactly those cells:\n\n%s\n\n"),
      tgt, format(sub$n_uncalled[1], big.mark = ","), paste(lines, collapse = "\n"))

    # The verdict depends on whether the scorers AGREE. Taking the worst scorer
    # and speaking for all of them would report a reference gap as ambiguity.
    if (nrow(unsure) == 0) {
      verdict <- "caution"
      msg <- paste0(msg, sprintf(paste(
        "**Every scorer stays fully confident there, so these cells are not intrinsically",
        "ambiguous -- %s simply has no marker set that covers them.** Treat this as a gap in",
        "%s's reference rather than as low-quality cells, and do not filter them out on the",
        "strength of the Unknown call."), tgt, tgt))
    } else if (nrow(sure) == 0) {
      verdict <- "note"
      msg <- paste0(msg, sprintf(paste(
        "**Every scorer is measurably less certain on exactly those cells**, so the methods",
        "are struggling on the same population. That is a genuinely ambiguous subset rather",
        "than a gap peculiar to %s -- expect no annotator to resolve it cleanly, and carry",
        "it as `Unknown` rather than forcing a label."), tgt))
    } else {
      verdict <- "important"
      msg <- paste0(msg, sprintf(paste(
        "**The scorers split, and that split is the finding.** %s is certain about these",
        "cells while %s is not. Confidence is measured against each classifier's own",
        "reference, so disagreement of this shape means the population is present in one",
        "reference and absent or poorly represented in the other -- it is a statement about",
        "**reference coverage, not about the cells**. Trust the annotator whose reference",
        "actually contains the tissue you sequenced, and read %s's low scores here as the",
        "same missing-population signal that made %s give up, not as evidence of ambiguity."),
        paste(sure$scorer, collapse = ", "), paste(unsure$scorer, collapse = ", "),
        paste(unsure$scorer, collapse = "/"), tgt))
    }
    scratch_finding(msg, type = verdict,
                    title = "Is low confidence where the annotators disagree?")
    scratch_table(rows[order(ratio),
                       .(scorer, `uncalled by` = uncalled_by, `n uncalled` = n_uncalled,
                         `median on uncalled` = median_on_uncalled,
                         `median on called` = median_on_called, ratio,
                         `p (Wilcoxon)` = signif(p_value, 3))],
                  caption = paste("Each scoring annotator's confidence on the cells another",
                                  "annotator left Unknown, versus the cells it named"))
  }
}
```
